topology_reasoning.device_identification: Symmetric three-waveguide adiabatic 1x2 splitter (trident/adiabatic coupler): one broad central input rail narrows to a terminating tip while two neighboring rails begin as narrow tips, broaden over the same transfer region, then separate through mirrored S-bends into two output guides.
topology_reasoning.operating_principle: The long, close, width-changing three-guide region transfers the central-guide input into the symmetric supermode of the two outer guides. The central rail vanishes adiabatically while the two outer rails grow; mirrored S-bends then fan the outer guides apart, yielding nominally equal outputs.
topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Use three independent gf.Path centerlines extruded on layer (1,0). Width transitions are primitive CrossSection transitions; the two outer centerlines are mirrored and use a smooth cubic Bezier S-bend. All function knobs are named top-level numeric assignments.

iterations.change_made: Initial measured three-path construction from the calibrated image. The diff shows small opposing edge bands from subpixel width/centerline differences, but the 0.85 acceptance threshold was exceeded, so iteration stopped as required.

validation_notes: The initial knob-proof attempt measured zero area because GDSFactory metadata made the $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ cell the sole top-level cell, which the evaluator intentionally excludes.
device.py was changed to write_gds(..., with_metadata=False). This serialization-only correction left the raster score unchanged and allowed the evaluator to measure the physical top cell.
